judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports independently identify the same core facts (registry.py cluster, staged ordering, F-06 as a policy decision, and the shared RESULTS_DB path) and hit all four expectations equally well; they are comparable in substance, with Report 1 slightly more detailed on integration/branching mechanics and Report 2 slightly more explicit about output-attribution risk from landing changes together.

report_1.evidence: Registry | Eng A | F-05, F-09 now; F-02 when the URL arrives | pipeline/registry.py ... Three findings (F-02, F-05, F-09) all edit the 11-line pipeline/registry.py... Splitting those across people guarantees conflicts; giving each hotspot one owner makes the parallelism real.

report_2.evidence: Engineer C — pipeline/registry.py cluster: F-09 and F-05 now, F-02 when unblocked. ... All three findings live in one 11-line file... pipeline/registry.py triple-booked. F-02, F-05, F-09 are three edits to one 11-line file — three separate PRs by three people is pure conflict churn.

report_1.evidence: Rubric | Eng B | F-11 (test first), then F-01 ... Registry | Eng A | F-05, F-09 now; F-02 when the URL arrives | pipeline/registry.py ... Runner | Eng C | F-12 (test first), then F-04(+F-13), then F-07, then F-14

report_2.evidence: Engineer B — pipeline/rubric.py cluster: F-01 plus F-11. ... Engineer C — pipeline/registry.py cluster: F-09 and F-05 now, F-02 when unblocked. ... Engineer A — pipeline/run_batch.py cluster: F-04+F-13, then F-14, then F-07, plus F-12.

report_1.evidence: F-06 — escalate, don't let an engineer guess. "Thresholds are too lenient; tighten them" names no target values. PARTIAL_CREDIT_THRESHOLDS = (0.35, 0.65) at score.py:3 directly sets production scores for every borderline answer — this is a product/behavior decision, not a mechanical fix... Get the numbers from the owner, then assign.

report_2.evidence: F-06 — do not hand to an engineer as written; it is a scoring-policy decision, not a bug fix. "Tighten them" specifies no target values, and PARTIAL_CREDIT_THRESHOLDS (score.py:3) determines every partial-credit score the pipeline emits — changing it silently re-scores all downstream results. It needs the rubric/metrics owner to pick values, ideally from a calibration run.

report_1.evidence: Shared test resource — tests/conftest.py:4 points the suite at a machine-global default, RESULTS_DB = /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db. Parallel test runs on a shared machine can collide unless each engineer overrides RESULTS_DB to a private path. ... A private RESULTS_DB: export RESULTS_DB=<own scratch path> before running tests, because tests/conftest.py:4 defaults to the machine-global /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db.

report_2.evidence: Shared local state. tests/conftest.py:4 defaults RESULTS_DB to the fixed path /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db — engineers sharing a machine or CI runner would collide unless each overrides the env var. ... RESULTS_DB env var set to a private path (e.g., under their own home/tmp), since tests/conftest.py defaults to the shared /var/tmp/llm-scoring/results.db.
